The 35-year-old shone for Michael Valkanis’ side in their 2026/27 A-League Men opener, scoring a sublime second goal to help the Roar defeat Perth Glory 2-1 at Suncorp Stadium. A 54-time South Korean international, Nam arrived in Queensland during the off-season as Valkanis and Co set about revitalising a Roar squad that finished second-last last season. “Yeah, [it was] my first game in [the] A-League and my first goal so, what can I say?” Nam said when fronting the media on Wednesday afternoon. “I’m so happy and I’m so happy to help the team win the game.” The Roar underwent a major off-season rebuild with 17 players leaving the club and 11 new faces coming through the door. Speaking in pre-season, Valkanis said his side would be adopting a different playing style compared to their more physical approach last season, with playmaker Nam seemingly key to their newfound identity. “Actually, he gives me like freedom, that’s what I I like,” Nam said when asked about his role in the side under Valkanis. “So I can move where the space [is]. I [can] find the space, I can move and I can create many chances and my teammates [have] helped me a lot. “So yeah, I’m enjoying so far. “Mostly I play as a number 10 position, and so with Brisbane, I think [it’s the] same role, and yeah, I’m happy to do that.” Not only is the South Korean International enjoying life on the field for the Roar, he’s also settling in quickly to a new city. “Yeah, I love it,” Nam smiled when asked about living in Brisbane. “I think one of best places to live, [in] my opinion. “A lot of Koreans in the city, you can find like Korean restaurants, also Korean cafes, and so I love it.” Nam will be back in action on Friday night when Brisbane Roar host reigning A-League Men champions Auckland FC at Suncorp Stadium. “I think the game will be difficult for us. Auckland are doing really well [the] last few years but we will do our best to make [it] difficult too. “Especially one of the legends of Japan, [Hiroki] Sakai. I never played against him yet, but on Friday it’s nice to play against the big players like Sakai.” A-League Men Subscribe to our newsletter Keep up with our latest news and events. Michael Valkanis’ side opened their campaign with a 2-1 win over Perth Glory last Friday. Justin Vidic struck before half-time and Nam Tae-hee doubled the lead with a volley from outside the box. Nine players made their A-League Men debuts on the night, including 18-year-old goalkeeper George Plusnin. Auckland arrive in Brisbane after a mixed start to their title defence. Under new head coach Pedro Moreira, they opened with a 3-1 home win over Melbourne City, with new signing Lachlan Bayliss scoring twice. Last week they were beaten 5-2 by Western Sydney Wanderers in Parramatta. Auckland will also head to Brisbane without striker Sam Cosgrove who has been suspended for Friday’s match. Auckland are captained by Japanese international Hiroki Sakai, who will come up against Roar midfielder and South Korean international Nam Tae-hee. Friday night is also Halloween Eve at Suncorp Stadium, and fans are encouraged to come in costume for their chance to win! Tickets available HERE! Team News Valkanis has named a 20-man squad, with academy graduates Niall Thom and Jordan Lauton promoted into the group. Dimitri Valkanis remains unavailable with a leg injury. Mike Tuckerman 28 October, 2026 Share Share Share this link via Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on X (Opens in new window) X Or Copy Link Copy Freelance football journalist, Mike Tuckerman returns to preview our clash with defending champions, Auckland FC this Friday night at Suncorp Stadium. If you’re only as good as your last game, then Brisbane Roar fans are pretty much looking at the best team in the A-League Men’s competition. The men in orange may have ridden their luck in the second half of last Friday’s 2-1 win over Perth Glory, but there were enough signs in the first half to suggest this new-look team will be tough to beat. In fact, there were so many positives it’s hard to know where to start. But let’s do so with Justin Vidic, who was deservedly named player of the match on the back of one of his most effective performances in orange. It wasn’t just that Vidic opened the scoring, peeling away from his marker to tap home Tate Russell’s intelligent cut-back just before the half-hour mark. Just as impressive was his relentless pressing on the night, which forced Glory to sit deep and spend much of the first half of the back foot. On another night, Vidic would have scored more than his solitary goal. But he was helped in no small part by Virgiliu Postolachi, whose near-post run dragged former Lions FC defender Cher Deng with him and opened the space for Vidic to tap home the opener. It was a vindication of coach Michael Valkanis’ decision to play two up top and a signal of attacking intent for the season ahead. Postolachi had plenty of good moments in a 65-minute A-League Men’s debut, before German import Marko Ilic came on and turned on the afterburners as he tormented the Glory defence. Ilic’s eye-catching runs down the left-hand side suggest the former TSV Havelse flyer will offer plenty in attack this season and should ensure the side maintains plenty of momentum in the second half of games. And if we’re singling out impressive attacking performers, how good was Nam Tae-hee? The former South Korean international was always going to show plenty of class, but few could have predicted just how well he’d control the tempo of the game in midfield. Nam looked a cut above in that first half against Perth, and he capped an assured display with an early contender for goal of the season when he deftly flicked up a Glory clearance before expertly dispatching it with an expertly taken volley from outside the box. If Nam stays fit, he’ll be one of the signings of the season. But there were plenty of others who looked the goods on the night – including, it’s worth pointing out, Joel King. Yes, the former Sydney FC defender would no doubt love to have his attempted back pass to debutant goalkeeper George Plusnin over again. But aside from that one mistake, both King and his right-sided counterpart Russell provided plenty of drive going forward and looked calm in defence. Plusnin himself was rarely tested in assured performance from the 18-year-old, and while Stefan Colakovski could have equalised midway through the second half, the fact that he sliced his one-on-one effort horribly wide suggests that even luck may be on Brisbane Roar’s side this season. One win doesn’t make a season, of course, but we saw enough in the season opener to suggest the Roar will cause plenty of headaches for opposition sides. Yet the visit of defending champions Auckland is another step up in quality, even if their English import Sam Cosgrove will miss Friday night’s showdown through suspension. The Kiwis still have plenty of talent – including former Newcastle Jets flyer Lachie Bayliss and All Whites international Logan Rogerson – and they’ll be out for redemption following their 5-2 mauling at the hands of Western Sydney Wanderers in Parramatta last week. AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND – OCTOBER 17: Lachlan Bayliss of Auckland FC celebrates after scoring a goal during the round one A-League Men match between Auckland FC and Melbourne City at Go Media Stadium, on October 17, 2026, in Auckland, New Zealand. (Photo by Hannah Peters/Getty Images) It all sets up another fascinating clash under the lights at Suncorp Stadium. Auckland won’t be easy. But on the basis of what we saw last Friday night, there’s no reason to doubt Brisbane Roar won’t take the game to the defending champions. Facebook Share on X (Opens in new window) X Or Copy Link Copy Fan Zone Match Preview Friday, October 30th, 10pm NZT Suncorp Stadium, Brisbane Written by Jonno Ross After missing out on the first round of the A League campaign due to match rescheduling, Brisbane Roar showed they were itching to get out on the park last weekend. After a busy off-season with player departures and arrivals, Roar fans would have been intrigued to see how their new-look, revamped team would shape up come opening day of their season. Brisbane did not disappoint. They came away with the three points after a 2-1 win over Perth Glory. The damage was done in the first half, thanks to goals from Justin Vidic and Nam Tae-hee. Perth looked set to stage a comeback, but couldn’t find the back of the Brisbane net. 2-1 to the home side, winning just their second opening game in the last ten seasons. Auckland FC will be looking to bounce back strongly this week. As we all know,  we suffered a disappointing 5-2 defeat to Western Sydney Wanderers last weekend. The defeat sent some supporters into panic, raising questions about the performance. Everyone needs to stay calm – one loss doesn’t define the season. It seemed like Auckland were going to kick on after winning their first game over Melbourne City. Luka Vicelich broke the deadlock with a stunning volley off a Francis de Vries cross, breaking the record for Auckland’s youngest ever goalscorer at just 18 years old.  The lead was cancelled out two minutes before halftime – one of the worst times to concede, and an absolute coach killer. It seemed to rattle the boys, coming out of the second half and conceding twice in a matter of minutes. Individual mistakes cost us, and the game was as good as over. A reality check for the players, who will look to right their wrongs on Friday night. It’s all about the response. Championship-winning teams are judged by how they react when things go wrong, and Auckland need to show that last weekend was a one-off rather than a sign of things to come. However, there’s one statistic Auckland supporters will be hoping continues . Auckland FC remain unbeaten against Brisbane Roar in competitive A-League fixtures, winning three of their four previous meetings, with the other ending in a draw. Both previous competitive visits to Brisbane have resulted in 2-0 victories for Auckland. Of course, past results count for little once the whistle blows. Brisbane will be determined to change that record, and Auckland can’t afford to underestimate them. The biggest concern for Auckland will be their defence. Conceding five goals last weekend is far from ideal, and Pedro Moreira will be looking for a much more disciplined performance from his backline. If Auckland can tighten things up defensively and take their chances going forward, there’s every reason to believe they can leave Brisbane with three points. Brisbane will be looking to make home advantage count, but Auckland have the quality to get a result. A win would be the perfect response to last weekend’s disappointment and another positive step in their title defence. The boys need to put the Wanderers result behind them, get back to basics and show the competition what they’re capable of. Players to Watch: Brisbane Roar – Nam Tae-hee The South Korean midfielder opened his account with a spectacular volley against Perth. His technical ability and eye for goal make him a dangerous opponent, and Auckland will need to ensure he doesn’t have too much time on the ball Auckland FC On Friday night, the attention won’t be on individual players. All eyes will be focused on how the side bounces back from last weekend’s defeat. Fans are calling out for a solid team performance. Auckland led through Vicelich from the 24th minute and held it until just before the break, but the hosts hit back with three goals in the space of seven minutes either side of the interval. The visitors dug in to pull it back to 3-2, only for two late Wanderers goals to stretch the margin and hand us a first defeat in five meetings with Western Sydney. It’s not the night we wanted, but there was fight in this young side right to the end. Opener: Luka Vicelich put Auckland FC ahead in the 24th minute, with Francis de Vries the provider from a corner. Swing around the break: Brandon Borrello levelled in the 43rd minute before Liam Gillion (46′) and Nicolas Milanović (50′) made it 3-1 to the hosts. Fightback: A Borrello own goal in the 68th minute cut the deficit to 3-2 and gave the travelling support fresh hope. Late goals: Miguel Di Pizio (86′) and substitute Atiya Waraga (89′) sealed the 5-2 result for the Wanderers. FIRST HALF Auckland FC lined up in a 4-4-2 at CommBank Stadium, with Michael Woud in goal, a back four of Francis de Vries, Nando Pijnaker, Luka Vicelich and Hiroki Sakai, and Sam Cosgrove and Lachlan Bayliss up front. The hosts had more of the ball early, but Auckland defended with real discipline and Lachlan Brook went close with a header from a de Vries cross in the 15th minute. A minute later de Vries tried his luck with a left-footed effort from outside the box, but Lawrence Thomas got down to his left to save. Auckland were the more threatening side in that spell, and the travelling support could sense something coming. It arrived in the 24th minute. From a corner, de Vries whipped in a cross and Vicelich met it with a right-footed shot from the centre of the box, sending it into the high centre of the goal. Auckland FC led 1-0, and what a moment for the defender. The hosts pushed back, with Dylan Scicluna testing the visitors from distance a few times without hitting the target, and Cosgrove had a header drift wide at the other end. Auckland held firm and went into the closing stages of the half still in front. Just before the break, though, the Wanderers hit back. Jake Brimmer forced a save from Thomas in the 43rd minute, but the hosts broke at speed and Scicluna set up Brandon Borrello to finish from the right side of the box. The half ended 1-1. SECOND HALF The hosts needed barely a minute to turn the match around. Liam Gillion struck in the 46th minute, a left-footed finish into the bottom left corner, and after Woud had kept out Borrello, Nicolas Milanović made it 3-1 in the 50th minute. That quick double changed the night for the visitors. Auckland did not fold. Logan Rogerson headed at Lawrence Thomas from a Hiroki Sakai cross, Lachlan Brook twice had efforts blocked, and Lachlan Bayliss dragged a shot wide from distance as the visitors pushed to get back into it. The Wanderers brought on Atiya Waraga in the 59th minute. Then came the lifeline. In the 68th minute, Brandon Borrello turned the ball into his own net to make it 3-2, and the travelling support had every reason to believe again. The hosts answered quickly, with Miguel Di Pizio hitting the bar from outside the box moments later. Pedro Miguel de Barros Moreira sent on fresh legs in the 71st minute, Daniel Normann and Van Fitzharris replacing Jake Brimmer and Lachlan Bayliss, but Auckland could not find the equaliser. Late on, the gap widened. Di Pizio finished from Dylan Scicluna’s pass on the break in the 86th minute, and substitute Waraga added a fifth in the 89th, set up by Aydan Hammond on another counter. Three minutes of added time passed, and the final whistle confirmed a 5-2 defeat. FULL TIME A 5-2 defeat at CommBank Stadium is not the night Auckland FC wanted, and it ends the club’s unbeaten record against the Wanderers after three wins and a draw in the four previous meetings. The numbers tell an honest story: the hosts held 61.9% of the ball to Auckland’s 38.1% and had 14 shots to our 9, with six on target to our four. Auckland were chasing the game for long stretches, and the Wanderers made the most of it, finishing with real sharpness in front of goal. We tip our hat to the hosts for that. There is still plenty to take from it. The opener showed what this side can do when it plays on the front foot, and the response to get back within a goal showed the resilience that has become part of this young club’s story. Auckland refused to drop their heads when the game could easily have run away from them, and that fight is something to build on. A young club still writing its story will have nights like this along the way, and the group will take the lessons, regroup quickly and get back to work. MATCH DETAILS Goals 24′ L. October 24 2026, 12:39 AM Delighted by the reaction of his players to falling behind on the scoreboard, Olivier Pantaloni spoke at the traditional post-match press conference following his side’s thrilling 2-1 away win over Brest. Coach, you must feel a great sense of satisfaction after this match, which started off going against you and was marked by a rather incredible match for your goalkeeper… Yes, an incredible match! And for Yéhvann (Diouf), it’s ended in the best possible way after a difficult start. We even wondered whether he’d be able to carry on, because mentally, it can really take its toll on a player – the goalkeeper’s role is a tricky one. When you make mistakes like that, it really hits you hard. The fact that the players immediately went over to him to support him, I think that gave him the strength to carry on and save that penalty at the end of the match. Did you doubt whether he’d be able to come back after the break? Not at half-time. I asked myself that question straight after the mistake; I spoke to my staff and the goalkeeping coach, who felt we should leave him on the pitch. Did you ask him how he was feeling at half-time? No. We discussed the fact that, from the moment he stayed on the pitch, there was that immediate show of support from the players and that, given we were behind, we needed to show our solidarity with Yéhvann and make sure we made up for his mistake by going on to secure a win. I think the players rose to the occasion. How would you assess your first-half performance, and how did the second half unfold more favourably? The first half was rather lacklustre, but in my view that was mainly down to our loss of possession and a significant lack of technical precision, because in terms of the game itself, I don’t feel we were put under any real pressure, apart from on a few long balls. But our defenders were able to cope with the intensity of the Brest forwards’ runs. In the second half, there was much more precision and movement. We also made some adjustments to the positioning of Gauthier (Hein) and Momo’ Amoura, who were playing a bit deeper, which meant we were able to link up better in midfield – something we hadn’t managed to do because they’d been playing far too high up in the first half. I think that allowed us to create more chances and ultimately led to this victory. When the penalty was awarded, did you think Diouf would save it? I didn’t think he’d save it, but I did think that, given what he’d been through in this match – the fact that we’d managed to come back and take the lead – he’d have the strength and the immense determination to save that penalty. That’s exactly what he managed to do. Do you think this favourable turn of events and the players’ reaction around Yéhvann will help you in your efforts to build a team? Absolutely. You are witnessing – especially this evening – that a team was growing and that it can achieve great things this season. As for Elye Wahi, we saw him offside quite a few times, but he still did you a favour by getting you back into the game… He’s the sort of player who, in a key moment, can turn a match around. In this instance, tonight (Friday), he enabled us to equalise. There were quite a few wasted chances in his play before that, but he’s so dangerous… He needs very few opportunities to be effective, and he proved that again tonight. What did you think of Sofiane Diop’s performance off the bench? You could sense he’d been champing at the bit a bit since he stopped being a first-team regular, but he’s continued to work hard and remain just as committed. He deserved to come on, and I think the goal he scored will do him a world of good going forward. Have you heard anything about Jonathan Clauss, who came off limping? He’s suffering from a sprained ankle. It might keep him out for a few weeks. Finally picking up points away from home is also very positive… We talked about it in the team talk – the fact that Nice hadn’t won away from home for quite some time. I simply told the lads that it wasn’t a foregone conclusion, that if we were determined to go out and get a win, we’d have to put certain things in place, and I think that’s exactly what they did in the second half.   Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Messenger E-mail Lien Back to top Share Print More on #sb29ogcn Olivier Pantaloni Post-match reactions First team Ligue 1 Related content Courageous Gym get dramatic win! A clash of extremes It will be a unique encounter between Le Havre and Paris this Friday evening, as the current bottom side in Ligue 1 host the league leaders. The Ciel & Marine, who have had a difficult start to the season, are still searching for their first win. However, the Le Havre side have held their own in certain games: in their away matches at Lyon (1–1) and Lille (1–0), as well as more recently away at Marseille (4–3). But now, the Normans need points. Points that Paris Saint-Germain have been racking up in recent weeks. Winning against Brest (0–1), Marseille (1–2), Le Mans (3–1) and Strasbourg (1–3), the Rouge et Bleu have shone on pitches across France and took advantage of their latest victory over Lyon (2–0) last Monday to take top spot in the table. With five consecutive wins in the top flight, Luis Enrique’s players head into this away fixture determined to continue their run and consolidate their position at the top of the table. The form in numbers 2 – Le Havre AC (131) and Paris Saint-Germain (163) are two of the three teams with the most shots in Ligue 1 this season, alongside Stade Brestois 29 (136). 12 – The capital club has lost just 12 per cent of its Ligue 1 matches against Le Havre (4 out of 34), a better record than against any other team they have faced at least as many times, apart from Brest (8 per cent). 14 – The Rouge et Bleu have scored in each of their last 14 away league matches, netting a total of 28 goals during that run. This is the best current run in the top flight. Seko, Ndiaye, Maja… Focus on the opposition In Le Havre’s goal, coach Didier Digard is expected to once again opt for Gauthier Gallon to cover for Lionel Mpasi’s absence. So far, the former Rennes goalkeeper has been preferred to Arnaud Bodart, who joined from Lille this summer, and the French goalkeeper should be able to rely on Ayumu Seko in front of him. The Japanese international acts as a linchpin in the Normandy side’s defence, where Junior Mwanga has established himself this season. The former Strasbourg midfielder is performing well in this role, whilst Algerian international Ahmed Touba is expected to complete a three-man central defence. At right-back, Timothée Pembélé is a major doubt for the clash against his former club. Danish international Elias Jelert, meanwhile, appears to be in contention for a return to the squad, though it remains unlikely he will start. This situation could once again propel the very young Djibril Ouziad (17) into the spotlight, whilst competition between Enzo Koffi and Lamine N’Diaye is fierce on the opposite flank. It is difficult to say which of the two defenders will start on the left-hand side, but whatever happens, HAC can count on Simon Ebonog to provide solidity in midfield. Having come through the Parisian academy, the Yaoundé-born player is expected to feature alongside Amir Richardson and Rassoul Ndiaye. On loan from Fiorentina and back in Seine-Maritime, the Moroccan international is a key figure in Le Havre’s midfield, whilst the Senegalese international, his team’s captain, brings both dynamism and leadership. The youngsters Daren Mosengo (20) and Guy-Noël Zohouri (19), meanwhile, are content with late-game appearances, and the same goes for new signing Kaito Mizuta, who has a more attacking profile. In attack, the Ciel & Marine certainly have no shortage of options. Starting with Josh Maja, who, after making a superb appearance off the bench in Marseille last week, is expected to regain his place in the starting line-up. It remains to be seen who will start alongside the Nigerian international. Whilst Rayan Fofana seems to be the frontrunner, the Ivorian international will still face competition from Mbwana Samatta, who has featured regularly since the start of the season, and from Japanese international Sota Nakamura. Notably, the Normandy side will still be without Felix Mambimbi, who has been out with an Achilles tendon injury since pre-season.

It’s important for us and for the supporters.” LE HAVRE “Every time we’ve been there or faced teams considered to be weaker, we’ve had problems. Even though we’re top of the table and they’re bottom, there will be difficult moments to manage during the match. It’s a test and a challenge for us. We have to continue to find sources of motivation to perform well. It’s never easy to go and play at Le Havre. They cause problems with their centre-forward and their wingers. They’re one of the teams in Ligue 1 that put in the most crosses. We have to show that we’re ready to overcome all that.” MATVEY SAFONOV “It’s simple: when he arrived, he faced the challenge of performing well at a top-flight club. He’s done everything right. He’s a perfect fit for what we’re looking for and for modern football. He plays a key role in the way we defend and in the way he builds play. We’re very pleased with him; he’s always looking to improve and is very courageous. I’m very pleased with the way he plays; he’ll continue to improve.” VITINHA “We know him well, so we’re not surprised. It’s a real pleasure to have a player with such technical and physical ability. His level is incredible. We’re very pleased to have a player of his calibre, even though he wasn’t ranked as highly as he deserves to be in the Ballon d’Or rankings.” THE INJURIES “We like to have as much control as possible, and the issue of injuries has been a major focus of our work in recent years. Some players suffer injuries more frequently than others, so it can sometimes be difficult to control. We aim to refine and optimise the training load to minimise the number of injured players. Throughout my coaching career, we’ve always sought to manage this; there have been tough times and better times, but I’m pleased with what we’re trying to achieve. However, it’s always difficult because injuries are part and parcel of top-flight football.”

Na een eerste helft met kansen aan beide kanten zette Van Zijl de Achterhoekse Trots met een prachtig afstandsschot op voorsprong. Lang leek die treffer voldoende voor de overwinning, maar in de 83e minuut kwam RKC Waalwijk alsnog langszij. De Graafschap begon met een mogelijkheid voor Donny Warmerdam, die na een dribbel van Toivo Mero vanaf de rand van het strafschopgebied over schoot. Aan de andere kant moest Kaya Symons een gevaarlijke inzet van dichtbij blokkeren. Kort daarna kreeg ook Fedde de Jong een grote kans na een uitbraak van Bjorn van Zijl, maar zijn schot ging over het doel. De Graafschap bleef mogelijkheden creëren. Een poging van Fedde de Jong uit een afvallende corner werd gepakt door doelman Niek Schiks. Vervolgens kwam Van Zijl dicht bij de openingstreffer, maar zijn schot vanaf de rand van het strafschopgebied belandde aan de buitenkant van de paal. Ook RKC Waalwijk kreeg kansen. Ties Wieggers redde op een kopbal bij de tweede paal, waarna meerdere schoten van de bezoekers werden geblokt. Finn Stokkers kopte uit een hoekschop naast het doel. In de 33e minuut was het vervolgens raak aan de andere kant. Van Zijl dribbelde vanaf rechts naar binnen en haalde van buiten het strafschopgebied uit met zijn linkerbeen. De bal krulde prachtig in de verre bovenhoek, buiten bereik van Schiks: 1-0. Vlak voor rust voorkwam Wieggers met een uitstekende redding op een vrije trap dat RKC Waalwijk langszij kwam. Na rust ging De Graafschap op zoek naar een tweede treffer. Van Zijl schoot naast en Mero kreeg een grote kans van dichtbij, maar zijn inzet werd geblokt. Ook een volgende uitbraak via Van Zijl leverde geen doelpunt op. Aan de andere kant hield Wieggers zijn ploeg op voorsprong met een redding op een schot van afstand. RKC Waalwijk bleef aandringen en kwam meerdere keren gevaarlijk voor het doel. Faissal Al Mazyani schoot net naast de verre bovenhoek, terwijl een poging van Stokkers na een aanraking naast ging. De Graafschap kreeg zelfs kansen om de voorsprong uit te breiden, maar onder meer Van Zijl en Mero kwamen niet tot scoren. In de slotfase bleef het spannend. Mero kreeg een grote mogelijkheid na een uitbraak en Warmerdam zag een schot voor het doel langs gaan. In de 83e minuut viel de gelijkmaker alsnog. Invaller Ryan Fage dribbelde naar binnen en schoot de 1-1 binnen. Een minuut later raakte hij ook nog de lat. RKC Waalwijk kreeg vervolgens nog een grote kopkans, maar de bal ging net over het doel van Wieggers. De Graafschap speelde uiteindelijk met 1-1 gelijk tegen RKC Waalwijk. De ploeg mag zich nu gaan richten op het bekerduel met Roda JC Kerkrade, dat aanstaande dinsdag op het programma staat. Vier Jahre später hat sich die SVE das Recht erkämpft, gegen die Profis in der Bundesliga zu spielen. Hinter dieser Erfolgsgeschichte stecken unter anderem kluge Transfer- und Personalentscheidungen sowie der stetige Glaube an die eigene Spielphilosophie. Wir blicken auf den Aufsteiger aus dem Saarland, ehe die 05ER zum ersten Freitagabendspiel der Saison (20:30 Uhr, live auf Sky & 05ER.fm ) an die Kaiserlinde reisen. Der Trainer Vincent Wagner hat, ähnlich wie sein jetziger Arbeitgeber, einen steilen Aufstieg hinter sich: Zur Saison 2022/23 übernahm der gebürtige Nordhäuser die Reservemannschaft der TSG 1899 Hoffenheim und führte sie innerhalb von drei Jahren in die dritthöchste Spielklasse. Zur ungefähr gleichen Zeit marschierte die SV Elversberg unter der Leitung von Horst Steffen von der vierten in die zweite Liga durch und scheiterte im zweiten Jahr denkbar knapp in der Bundesliga-Relegation am 1. FC Heidenheim.  Steffen zog es zu Beginn der Spielzeit 2025/26 weiter nach Bremen – Wagner trat das schwere Erbe an und führte die SVE in seiner Debüt-Saison in die Bundesliga. Im Fußball-Oberhaus angekommen, hält der 40-Jährige weiter an seiner Spielidee fest: Hohes, aggressives Pressing gepaart mit schnellem Umschaltspiel und einer Abwehrreihe, die stets nach vorne verteidigt – "Power-Fußball" nennt Wagner seine taktische Ausrichtung: "Unser Ziel ist es, mit aktivem Fußball die Klasse zu halten. Da werden wir höchstwahrscheinlich an der ein oder anderen Stelle an unsere Grenzen stoßen – dennoch sehe ich diesen Weg als alternativlos. Das war stets meine Philosophie und das werde ich auch nicht ändern“, so der Cheftrainer vor der Saison über sein Vorhaben. Der Förstersohn mit Fußballexpertise: Vincent Wagner (Foto: IMAGO/ Picture Point LE). Der Kader Einen Umbruch, so wie es bei den meisten Aufsteigern der Fall ist, gab es im Saarland nicht. Der Kern der Mannschaft blieb Wagner erhalten, vor allem in der Defensivabteilung. Im Tor ist Nicolas Kristof gesetzt. Der 26-Jährige erlebte den rasanten Aufstieg von Liga vier bis in die Bundesliga mit – genauso wie Stürmer Luca Schnellbacher. Auch Kapitän und Abwehrchef Lukas Pinckert ist ein alt eingesessener Hase, der in der Spielzeit 2022/23 zu den Saarländern kam. Im Zentrum steht ihm Maximilian Rohr zur Seite, sowie Lasse Günther, Jan Gyamerah und Neuzugang Luca Sirch auf den Außenpositionen. Im defensiven Mittelfeld tummelt sich ein weiteres neues Gesicht: Lukasz Poreba, gekommen vom HSV, soll an der Seite von Felix Keidel die letzte Linie vor der Verteidigung bilden. Aufgerüstet hat die SVE vor allem in der Offensive: Die neue "junge Garde" beginnt vor allem bei Königstransfer Cole Campbell. Das 20-jährige Talent wurde vor der Saison für eine Ablöse von sechs Millionen fest verpflichtet – ebenso wie das ehemalige Bayern-Talent Maurice Krattenmacher für rund zwei Millionen. Zudem wurden Francis Onyeka, Noah Darvich und Noel Futkeu ausgeliehen. David Mokwa, Lukas Petkov und Tom Zimmerschied ziehen da den Altersschnitt schon ein wenig in die Höhe, genießen jedoch weiterhin vollstes Vertrauen vom Cheftrainer. Vor allem Mokwa hat ein langjähriges Verhältnis zu Wagner: Er spielte bereits in Hoffenheim unter dem 40-Jährigen und hat sich nun zu einer absoluten Stammkraft entwickelt.  Traf direkt beim Bundesligadebüt für die Elv: Königstransfer Cole Campbell (Foto: IMAGO/ Fussball-News Saarland). Der Saisonstart Spektakulär startete die SVE in ihre Debüt-Saison: Am ersten Spieltag besiegte die Wagner-Elf Bayer 04 Leverkusen vor heimischem Publikum mit 3:2. Eine Woche später drehten sie binnen 30 Minuten einen 1:3-Rückstand im Borussia-Park und besiegten Borussia Mönchengladbach letztendlich mit 4:3. Auch gegen die Bayern ließ sich die Elf von der Kaiserlinde nicht den Schneid abkaufen und unterlag nur knapp mit 1:2 gegen den Rekordmeister. Nach der Länderspielpause verflachte das Momentum des "Power-Fußballs" ein wenig – es folgte ein torloses Remis auf Schalke und einer knappe 0:1-Niederlage an der alten Försterei. Gegen den FC Augsburg berauschte sich der Aufsteiger dann aber wieder am Wagner-Fußball. Nach einem wilden Hin und Her konnte die SVE ihren dritten Saisonsieg einfahren und sprang durch den 4:3-Erfolg gegen den FCA zwischenzeitlich auf Tabellenplatz sechs. Vergangenes Wochenende setzte es eine 0:4-Auswärtsniederlage bei den heimstarken Leipzigern, sodass die SVE vor diesem Spieltag Rang acht in der Tabelle belegt. Im Pokal musste die Wagner-Elf in der zweiten Runde die Segel streichen - und teilte dabei das Schicksal der 05ER: Sie mussten sich ebenfalls einem Zweitligisten geschlagen geben. Gegen den SV Darmstadt 98 setzte es vor heimischen Publikum eine 0:2-Niederlage. Ließ beim letzten Gastspiel an der Kaiserlinde hinten nichts anbrennen: Danny Da Costa (li.). Das letzte Mal Neben Oberliga-Duellen in den 80er-Jahren trafen die beiden Mannschaften zweimal im DFB-Pokal aufeinander – beide Male gingen die 05ER siegreich vom Platz. Das jüngste Duell fand vor drei Jahren statt: In der ersten Runde des Pokalwettbewerbs erzielte Ludovic Ajorque den goldenen Treffer zum 1:0-Auswärtssieg.  Gegen die U23 des FSV gab es deutlich mehr Partien. In insgesamt 23 Begegnungen, verteilt auf verschiedene Regionalliga-Staffeln, spricht die Bilanz für die Elf von der Kaiserlinde: Zehn Siege, sieben Unentschieden und sechs Niederlagen stehen dabei aus Sicht der Saarländer zu Buche – diese Statistik wird sich höchstwahrscheinlich in naher Zukunft nicht verändern. Au sortir d’une séance ouverte au public qui a réuni plus de 3 500 supporters sang et or à l’occasion des vacances scolaires, le coach Yannick Cahuzac et Samson Baidoo se sont présentés en conférence de presse, ce mercredi. Le moment d’aborder le derby de vendredi (21h05). Publié le 28/10/2026 à 13:38 Temps de lecture : 7 min. Sur le groupe « Odsonne Édouard a subi une petite intervention chirurgicale ce matin, il avait des douleurs chroniques depuis le début de saison qui l’empêchaient d’être à son meilleur niveau. En accord avec le staff, il a subi cette intervention qui l’éloignera des terrains durant quelques semaines. Parmi les autres absents, on a toujours Maik Nawrocki et Ismaelo Ganiou , qui a subi une intervention aussi et qui était de retour ce matin à La Gaillette. Cela nous a fait plaisir de le voir. Le reste du groupe est disponible. C’est un coup dur pour Odsonne. Mais comme pour tous les autres blessés qui ont subi des interventions ces derniers temps, le staff et le club dans son ensemble seront là pour l’accompagner et l’aider à revenir au plus vite. Odsonne est très pointilleux dans le fait d’être performant. Il avait trop de gênes constamment pour ne pas subir cette intervention. On souhaite qu’il soit vite de retour pour nous aider. » Yannick Cahuzac Sur Samson Baidoo « Je suis très heureux de retrouver l’équipe et les terrains. Ce n’était pas facile pour moi d’être éloigné de la compétition, j’ai dû traverser des difficultés avec ma blessure. J’espère revenir au fur et à mesure à 100 % de mes capacités. La dernière blessure n’était pas facile mais avec la volonté et la patience, on finit par y parvenir. J’ai toujours été régulier mais beaucoup plus depuis que j’ai eu ces blessures, je fais davantage de prévention, des exercices en salle, je travaille avec le staff, je fais d’autant plus attention à mon hygiène de vie en dehors des terrains. » « L’objectif est de garder cette bonne défense à trois, c’est vrai qu’il y a eu pas mal de blessures récemment, comme Ismaelo Ganiou, Jonathan Gradit ou moi. Sur le terrain, on est parfois accompagnés de Kyllian Antonio, Jean-Clair Todibo, ou d’autres très bons défenseurs. Parfois les blessures touchent les défenseurs, parfois d’autres secteurs. C’est le jeu, on fait avec. » Samson Baidoo Sur le coach Yannick Cahuzac « Je pense que le coach, Yannick Cahuzac, sait certainement beaucoup plus de choses sur le club que nous, joueurs, donc on considère que c’est le coach qui nous donne les meilleurs conseils. Il nous demander de jouer avec solidarité, avec le cœur. C’est quelque chose qui nous correspond et qui correspond au club. » Samson Baidoo « Enchaîner les matchs tous les trois jours demande énormément d’efforts, surtout psychologiquement. J’ai aussi la chance de faire un métier extraordinaire, mais il est vrai que préparer un match sur une semaine complète est positif. Je trouve que l’équipe progresse. On avance dans le jeu, on est sur une forme de continuité dans le travail. C’est ce qui va nous permettre d’aller le plus loin possible. J’ai un staff très performant, compétent, qui est là pour m’appuyer. Ils sont importants pour moi et l’ensemble du groupe. » Yannick Cahuzac Sur le derby « Bien sûr, le derby est dans nos têtes car c’est un match important. C’est toujours diff quand on joue Lille, on veut donner évidemment bonne figure et se donner à 100 %, tant individuellement que collectivement. C’est un rendez-vous important pour tout le club. On a envie de montrer vendredi qu’on est prêts pour ce match. » Samson Baidoo « Un derby est toujours un match avec une saveur particulière, surtout ici. On sait l’importance de ce match pour nos supporters et la région. On va s’atteler à tout mettre en œuvre vendredi pour les rendre fiers. Ce qui est important pour moi - pour avoir vécu pas mal de derbies (5, ndlr) - c’est de répondre présents le jour J sans jouer le match avant. Rien ne sert de faire monter l’excitation. Il faut le préparer sereinement pour maîtriser au mieux nos émotions. On sait que ce sera intense, certainement électrique. Il faudra rester disciplinés et répondre présents dans l’intensité. » « Ce sera un match engagé face à un bel adversaire qui est dans les trois premiers. On va vraiment se concentrer sur nous et ensuite on essaiera de teinter nos principes en fonction de l’adversaire. Fora de ação desde abril, quando sofreu uma lesão multiligamentar após uma entrada dura de Quintero, na partida contra a LDU, pela Libertadores, o jogador comemora a evolução, mas ainda não tem uma data definida para voltar a jogar. ✅ Clique aqui e siga o canal do ge Mirassol no WhatsApp! 1 de 3Negueba volta a treinar com bola pelo Mirassol — Foto: Divulgação/Mirassol Negueba volta a treinar com bola pelo Mirassol — Foto: Divulgação/Mirassol A recuperação vem avançando conforme o planejamento do departamento médico. Com três meses de cirurgia, Negueba já caminhava sem muletas pelo CT, utilizava a esteira antigravidade e realizava exercícios na bicicleta ergométrica. Agora, o atacante começa a intensificar as atividades no gramado. Segundo o médico do Mirassol, Francys França, a evolução é positiva, embora a previsão de retorno permaneça entre 9 e 12 meses após o procedimento. Para Negueba, a possibilidade de voltar a realizar atividades em campo representa um dos momentos mais aguardados desde a cirurgia. O atacante também destacou as reflexões durante o período afastado do futebol. — Estou muito feliz por ter passado por esse processo tão longo e chegado a esse momento que, como muitos falam, é a parte boa, quando começam os trabalhos em campo. Você fica um tempo fora dos gramados, começa a pensar um pouco mais no extracampo e aproveita mais a família e os filhos. — Agora é dar sequência, seguir o protocolo e, em breve, estar de volta aos gramados para dar alegria ao nosso torcedor novamente. 3 de 3Atacante Negueba volta treinar no campo pelo Mirassol — Foto: Divulgação/Mirassol Atacante Negueba volta treinar no campo pelo Mirassol — Foto: Divulgação/Mirassol Mesmo acompanhando a rotina do Mirassol durante a recuperação, Negueba reconheceu que sente falta de participar das partidas, das viagens e até dos momentos de concentração com os companheiros. — Tenho um pouco de saudade, mas ainda não estou com aquela ansiedade tão grande. Guanaes lamenta chances perdidas pelo Mirassol contra o São Paulo: "Era para estar 4 a 0" Treinador cita volume antes da pausa para a hidratação, mas diz que é importante valorizar o empate Por Gabriel Castro — Mirassol, SP 25/10/2026 06h40 Atualizado 25/10/2026 Mirassol 1 x 1 São Paulo | melhores momentos | 32ª rodada | Brasileirão 2026 Após o empate por 1 a 1 com o São Paulo, na noite deste sábado, o técnico Rafael Guanaes lamentou as oportunidades desperdiçadas pelo Mirassol , mas valorizou o ponto conquistado na luta contra o rebaixamento. — Minha leitura do jogo é que nós perdemos dois pontos, mas preciso valorizar esse um ponto. Perdemos dois pontos porque criamos muito, tivemos um jogo muito bem desenhado. Fizemos 1 a 0 e, até a parada, era um jogo para estar 4 a 0, com todo o respeito ao adversário. Tivemos muitas chances contra um time muito forte, que em algum momento teria uma oportunidade. Precisávamos ser mais eficientes. 1 de 3Rafael Guanaes no duelo entre Mirassol e São Paulo — Foto: JP Pinheiro/Agência Mirassol Rafael Guanaes no duelo entre Mirassol e São Paulo — Foto: JP Pinheiro/Agência Mirassol ✅ Clique aqui e siga o canal do ge Mirassol no WhatsApp! Guanaes destacou os primeiros 35 minutos do Mirassol, quando a equipe controlou a partida e criou oportunidades para ampliar o placar. — Começamos muito bem, tivemos uns 35 minutos praticamente perfeitos, com o jogo totalmente controlado e muitas chances. O Rafael saiu como o melhor em campo. No segundo tempo, retomamos o controle e criamos alternativas para buscar a vitória. Veja também + Mirassol desperdiça chances, falha na defesa e fica no empate + Mirassol 1x1 São Paulo: veja como foi Apesar da frustração, o treinador ressaltou a evolução do Mirassol e a capacidade de competir com os grandes clubes da Série A. Para ele, a insatisfação da torcida com o empate diante do São Paulo demonstra a mudança de patamar da equipe. — A gente jogou contra o São Paulo e o torcedor saiu frustrado porque não vencemos, pelo futebol que apresentamos. Isso mostra o quanto conseguimos mudar o nível do Mirassol em relação aos clubes da Série A. Chegar a um jogo como esse, enfrentar um time grande de igual para igual, com coragem, e ainda ter a possibilidade de ser superior e vencer é um legado que me deixa muito feliz. Com o empate, o time amarelo e verde chegou aos 37 pontos e dorme na 15ª posição, e o treinador reforçou a meta de alcançar os 45 pontos nas seis rodadas restantes. — Fica uma frustração pela quantidade de chances criadas, mas, ao mesmo tempo, é mais um ponto na Série A que nos aproxima da nossa meta. Matematicamente, estamos mirando os 45 pontos, temos 37, faltam oito e ainda existem muitos confrontos diretos. Esse corte vai ser no meio dessa disputa, mas vamos continuar focados nos 45. 2 de 3Mirassol x São Paulo pelo Brasileir — Foto: Joisel Amaral/AGIF Mirassol x São Paulo pelo Brasileir — Foto: Joisel Amaral/AGIF Com quatro dos seis compromissos restantes fora de casa, o treinador também destacou a necessidade de manter a postura ofensiva como visitante, sem deixar de reconhecer o desgaste acumulado ao longo da temporada. Time enfrenta ainda Corinthians, Chapecoense, Fluminense e Grêmio fora de casa. — Precisamos de pontos. Não podemos ir para os jogos pensando apenas em beliscar um pontinho, porque talvez isso não resolva nossa situação. Temos que enfrentar os adversários com coragem e, se não der para ganhar, somar um ponto importante, como aconteceu agora. Por isso, prefiro exaltar o ponto. – Conseguimos uma ótima recuperação no segundo turno e estamos no caminho certo pelo futebol que apresentamos. Temos seis decisões pela frente, duas em casa e quatro fora. Existe um desgaste notório chegando ao fim da temporada, então precisamos equilibrar isso para estar com o tanque cheio e disputar esses jogos no nosso limite. 3 de 3Rafael Guanaes na partida entre Mirassol e São Paulo — Foto: Joisel Amaral/AGIF Rafael Guanaes na partida entre Mirassol e São Paulo — Foto: Joisel Amaral/AGIF Por fim, Guanaes projetou o confronto com o Corinthians e apontou a dificuldade de analisar as possíveis mudanças no adversário, já que o novo treinador Seedorf tem apenas o jogo do Vasco na beira do campo. — Esse jogo contra o Corinthians é o mais difícil de planejar, porque, apesar de conhecermos os jogadores, o treinador só conhece realmente o elenco e o contexto quando começa a trabalhar no dia a dia. É difícil identificar tão rapidamente o que já mudou em termos táticos, e eles terão uma semana para trabalhar. — Temos esses dois jogos como amostra e vamos mergulhar neles para planejar bem a partida. Precisamos prever possíveis mudanças de escalação e de modelo de jogo, mas também focar muito naquilo que queremos fazer. Mesmo fora de casa, vamos tentar colocar em prática o nosso futebol – finalizou o treinador. O Mirassol volta a campo nesta sexta-feira, às 20h, quando enfrenta o Corinthians, em São Paulo, pela 33ª rodada do Campeonato Brasileiro.
